hook_text: In the early 2000s, South Africans' life expectancy dropped by almost ten years. Then it climbed back. Here's why.
clip_script: HIV weakens the body's defences. In the early 2000s, before treatment reached most people, AIDS killed hundreds of thousands of South Africans a year, and life expectancy fell to about fifty-three. Then came ARVs, the world's biggest treatment programme, and life expectancy climbed back above sixty-five. TB, spread by coughing, is curable with six months of daily pills. Malaria, carried by mosquitoes, kills mostly young children in Africa, but nets and spraying cut it down. And diarrhoea, from dirty water, can be beaten with soap, toilets, and a simple drink of clean water, sugar and salt. Knowledge saves lives.
visual_style: A life expectancy line for South Africa dips sharply then rises; four icons appear in turn: a red ribbon, a pair of lungs, a mosquito, and a water drop with soap bubbles.
pacing: A steady build to the turning point, then a confident close.
